rationale: Recording the contrast that explains why the finding is about classification rather than about unauthenticated messages in general, which a reviewer will ask. Step treats a message with no term as a local message and skips every term comparison, so for message types that legitimately travel the network (MsgApp, MsgHeartbeat, MsgSnap) a peer could in principle reach stepFollower with term 0 as well and have the follower adopt it as leader and reset its election timer. That path needs an illegal term that no correct peer produces, and it self-heals on the next real leader message; the local-only types are the ones the module can and does filter, and MsgForgetLeader is the single one missing from that set, which is why the finding stands on classification rather than on the absence of message authentication.

knowledge.statement: Step skips all term handling for a message whose term is zero, treating it as a local message, and then dispatches on its type: for MsgApp, MsgHeartbeat and MsgSnap that reaches stepFollower, which sets the election timer to zero and adopts m.From as the leader before handling the payload. So term-zero trust is not specific to MsgForgetLeader; what is specific to it is that it is the only locally-produced type missing from the inbound filter, so it reaches that trust from a peer with no illegal field at all, while a peer would have to send MsgApp or MsgHeartbeat with an illegal zero term to reach the same state change. That illegal-term path is not a correct-peer behaviour, its effect is bounded (a follower's advertised leader and timer, with a divergent uncommitted tail that the next real leader truncates) and it needs no classification change to be described.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution claimed): raft.go 1094-1100 (the term switch whose first case is the local-message case) and 1730-1739 (stepFollower setting electionElapsed and lead for MsgApp, MsgHeartbeat and MsgSnap). The contrast assumes a follower already at a term of at least 1, which every node reaches through becomeFollower(1, None) before it can lead or vote; the finding it clarifies is the main question's, whose evidence is the receipts cited there.
